source.title: Measuring Mathematical Problem Solving With the MATH Dataset
source.authors: Dan Hendrycks; Collin Burns; Saurav Kadavath; Akul Arora; Steven Basart; Eric Tang; D. Song; Jacob Steinhardt

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It measures downstream MATH accuracy across model sizes, rather than held-out pretraining loss or compute-optimal allocations.
record.gate_note: The study tests exact-match answer accuracy on MATH, not held-out cross-entropy. Scaling results from other papers are cited but are not this study’s results. AMPS and solution-training comparisons are not rows for the versions here because they do not test the specified size/loss predictability claim.
record.test_reason: The study's own Table 2 reports MATH exact-match accuracy for a GPT-2 size sweep (0.1B–1.5B, all AMPS-pretrained and MATH-fine-tuned) and a GPT-3 few-shot pair (13B, 175B). These results bear on V6, whether downstream performance improves predictably with scale. The authors also extrapolate a log-linear trend. The paper does not measure pretraining loss, allocation or architecture shape.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors find MATH accuracy rises only slowly with model size (5.4% to 6.9% over 15x parameters), unlike most text tasks. Assuming a log-linear trend, about 10^35 parameters would be needed for 40%, so they argue algorithmic advances are needed. They also report that AMPS pretraining matches about a 130x parameter increase.
record.recipe_differences: Uses exact-match downstream benchmark accuracy across model sizes, rather than fitting held-out language-model loss laws or measuring compute-optimal parameter/token allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported accuracy differs across MATH subjects; comparisons also vary in evaluation setup, including fine-tuning versus few-shot evaluation.

fits_no_version.finding: AMPS math pretraining lets a 0.1B GPT-2 match a fine-tuned 13B GPT-3 without AMPS (5.4% vs 5.2%); the authors equate this to a 130x parameter increase.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Domain-specific pretraining data can substitute for orders of magnitude of parameters on downstream reasoning accuracy.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2021 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for these accuracy results. The model-size trend is described as slow, category-level values are uneven, and the large-size forecast is not tested on an actual run. The table mixes fine-tuned and few-shot GPT-3 results, so those configurations are not a single controlled size sweep.
record.rows_left_out: None. Table 2’s separately reported subject-category and average accuracy results are included, as are the stated extrapolation and AMPS comparison values relevant to downstream accuracy and scale.

untested.parts: Predictability from pretraining loss. No curve fit to accuracy versus size is reported. The extrapolation is not validated against a larger run. The GPT-2 sweep covers only 15x in parameters.
Not tested: no pretraining loss measured.
Not tested (the BART-versus-GPT comparison is not at fixed parameter count with controlled shape).

missing.what: Accuracy by difficulty level for GPT-2 0.1B versus 1.5B, overall and per subject (1.5B about 15% at level 1, about 4% at level 5).
UnifiedQA model sizes versus LogiQA accuracy, rising with size; authors say it will soon be solved by scale. Values must be read off the figure.
BART-Large 0.4B (AMPS-pretrained) gets 4.9% on MATH, below GPT-2 0.1B.

record.verdict_notes: The per-subject differences are about one percentage point with no uncertainty reported, so the per-category reversals are weak evidence. The GPT-3 fine-tuned and few-shot rows are not comparable to the GPT-2 sweep because pretraining and evaluation differ. The paper cites Kaplan et al. but is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law relation in parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No small-run loss fit is tested against the loss of larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameters and tokens is tested.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No other modality or training regime is tested for the same loss law.
Tests downstream MATH accuracy versus model size only; it does not test predictability from pretraining loss or validate extrapolations on much larger runs.
Does not investigate fitted loss exponents, compute-optimal splits, or fitting/setup dependence of those laws.
